title: Vacuum cleaner
body:
An ordinary student day.
The morning wake-up—though brutal—motivated me to organize the rest of my day. So I decide, after an "educational" obligation, to clean the house.
I tidy up my things and clothes, wash a few dishes left over from last night, run a load of laundry, go to the supermarket for two or three things I was missing, clean my guitars, dust the furniture. A lot of work already, and I hadn't even touched the vacuum cleaner yet.
Its time had come.
It was waiting for me patiently in its spot—placed in a strange, crooked posture because my apartment isn't famous for its roominess...
I pull the cord, plug it in. Suddenly, without any recent similar experience, it hits me and I start sneezing uncontrollably. And again. And again. To the point where I got tired, left the vacuum as it was, and sat down to calm down.
Usually such allergies affect me, but not so abruptly!
Having relative calm restored, I return to the job and notice that the vacuum itself is covered in dust! I realize I had dusted every corner of the house except for the vacuum itself; and naturally, this small detail drained part of my strength, as it triggered an inexplicable, endless sneezing fit.
We all know that the role of a vacuum is to sweep. To clean. To bind all the useless matter covering the floor, including dust.
It isn't a given, however, that the vacuum itself is clean, wiped down!

Many times, we are so "crazy" about our roles;
about our obligations toward our environment;
about the rules;
that we forget to care for ourselves.
We forget to "dust" ourselves from the "dust" we absorb from others.

We forget to give time and space to ourselves;
to rest him soul and body;
to nourish and water him properly;
to wash him properly;
to love him.
Because when we don't, we lose our energy from that reflexive "sneeze" that tells us:
"WHOA, YOU'RE DOING SOMETHING WRONG BRO."
Dust your vacuum cleaner often.

y.f.
